summary: Frontend-only regression + feature testing for refined Goorin B2B Ops Dashboard. Executed 46 assertions across login/skeleton, topbar (cart badge=2, cart -> Marketplace, account chip 'Ryan M / AS / Mirabile Distribution', search placeholder), account strip, YTD/trailing spend toggle + bars + tooltip, quick actions, shipments widget, announcements widget (all 3 links + navigation), Recent/All Orders drawer flows (SO56680 timeline, tracking, line items, balance due, invoice-success toast; SO58739 not-invoiced info toast; SO54102 cancelled label), drawer close via X/Escape/backdrop, reorder navigation, contact-rep, search empty-state + clear buttons. All scenarios listed in the review request PASS. Only one minor data inconsistency found (see below).

issues: Trailing-12-month spend series is offset by one month vs YTD data. Hovering spend-bar-apr shows 'Apr · $282.00', but that value is actually March's real spend; the real April 2026 total ($1,692 from SO54871) shows up under May. Review request expected 'Apr · $1,692.00'. In DashboardPage.tsx line 61: trailingSpend = [420, 610, 0, 380, 846, 0, 282, 1692, 0, 564, 1128, 51] with trailingMonths starting at Oct — the last 9 slots should mirror ytdSpend (846, 0, 282, 1692, 0, 564, 1128, 34, 17) but are shifted by 1. Purely cosmetic since data is mocked, but the two views disagree.

action_items: Fix trailingSpend offset in /app/frontend/src/DashboardPage.tsx line 61 so Jan..Sep values match ytdSpend (currently shifted by one month, causing Apr tooltip to show $282 instead of $1,692).
critical_code_review_comments: DashboardPage.tsx line 358 still hardcodes '7d ago' relative time — will drift; compute from orders[0].date (carried over from iteration_1).

SpendBars uses data-testid={`spend-bar-${label.toLowerCase()}`}; safe today because trailingMonths has unique months, but if the 12-mo window ever includes duplicate month names, testids will collide. Consider suffixing with index.
OrderDrawer 'Paid to date' logic (line 114) hardcodes half of total for 'Partially Paid' — fine for mock, but should be data-driven when wired up.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (46/46 assertions pass, 1 minor data inconsistency logged)
